name: Pennsylvania
headline_status: Medical cannabis is legal in Pennsylvania, but recreational use is still illegal statewide.
summary: Pennsylvania's Medical Marijuana Act, signed April 17, 2016, lets patients with one of 24 qualifying conditions buy cannabis from licensed dispensaries, which began selling in February 2018. Recreational cannabis remains illegal: possessing 30 grams or less is a misdemeanor punishable by up to 30 days in jail. The House passed a state-store legalization bill (HB 1200) in May 2025, but a Senate committee killed it, and on June 10, 2026 the Senate voted 27-23 against SB 49, which would have created a Cannabis Control Board and regulated intoxicating hemp.

medical_since.value: April 17, 2016, when the Medical Marijuana Act (Act 16) was signed.

medical_program.value: Patients with one of 24 qualifying serious medical conditions need a certification from an approved practitioner and must register with the Department of Health.

retail_sales.value: Medical dispensaries have sold to registered patients and caregivers since February 2018; there are no adult-use sales.

possession_limit.value: No legal possession amount for adults without a medical card.

penalties.value: 30 g or less of marijuana (8 g of hashish) is a misdemeanor punishable by up to 30 days in jail and a $500 fine; larger amounts carry heavier misdemeanor penalties. First offenders may qualify for conditional release.

regulator.value: Office of Medical Marijuana, Pennsylvania Department of Health.

hemp_thc.value: Intoxicating hemp products are unregulated at the state level, according to the Shapiro administration; a bill to regulate them (SB 49) failed in the Senate in June 2026.

purchase_age.value: Medical only. Patients under 18 get medical marijuana through a registered caregiver, who generally must be 21 or older; patients and caregivers must be Pennsylvania residents.

public_use.value: There is no legal recreational use anywhere. Registered patients may vaporize dried leaf but are still prohibited from smoking medical marijuana.

dui.value: Zero tolerance: Pennsylvania is among the states that ban driving with any amount of THC or its metabolites in the body.

tourists.value: No. Only Pennsylvania residents with a state driver's license or ID can register as patients, so out-of-state medical cards cannot be used to buy, and there are no adult-use sales.

home_grow.value: Not permitted, including for registered patients.

faq.a: Only for registered medical patients. Recreational marijuana is illegal statewide, though legalization bills keep being debated in Harrisburg.

faq.q: What is the penalty for weed possession in Pennsylvania?
faq.a: Possessing 30 grams or less is a misdemeanor with up to 30 days in jail and a $500 fine; larger amounts bring heavier penalties.

faq.q: How do you get a medical marijuana card in Pennsylvania?
faq.a: Get certified by a Department of Health-approved practitioner for one of 24 qualifying conditions, then register with the state's medical marijuana program.
